about: The pointer's gestures on cells: click, Shift+click and drag, Ctrl+click adding and taking out, Ctrl+A. From tests/ExGrid.Tests/SelectionGestureTests.cs.

cases.name: ADR-0012/0052: a click makes the cell the Focus and the Extent, and the selection collapses to it
ADR-0052: Shift+click keeps the Focus, moves the Extent to the clicked cell and redraws the range
ADR-0052: extending past the far side flips the range around the Focus
ADR-0052 case 2: a drag's Focus is where the button went down, whichever way it moves: D5 to B2 leaves D5
ADR-0012/0052: Ctrl+click adds a range holding the Focus
ADR-0052 case 5: Ctrl+click D5 onto A1:B2, then Shift+Down gives A1:B2,D5:D6
ADR-0011/0052: Ctrl+A is one rectangle over every row and every visible column, and the Focus does not move
ADR-0011: Ctrl+A from nothing selected puts the Focus on the first cell

ADR-0012/0052 third run: Ctrl+click on a selected cell takes it out of every range holding it, each giving way in place to its fragments bottom to top, and the Focus goes to the first remaining cell, by rows, of the range made last
ADR-0052 case 6: B2 out of A1:C3 (A1 active) keeps A1 active, and Shift+Down extends A1:C1 to A1:C2
ADR-0052 case 6 / third run: A1 out of A1:C3 moves the Focus to B1, the first remaining cell by rows, and Shift+Down extends B1:C1
ADR-0052 / SL-5 (the seventeenth Windows run, h4): A1:B2, F6, F6 again empties the range made last; A1:B2 takes its place with the Focus on A1, and Enter cycles it with the selection kept
ADR-0052 case 6: the only selected cell cannot be taken out
ADR-0012: nothing selected has no Focus, no Extent and no Focus range, rather than answering (0, 0)
ADR-0012: Shift+click with nothing selected is a click: there is no Focus
ADR-0012: Ctrl+click with nothing selected selects the cell
